correctness.rationale: For every n≥3, 1≤r≤n, 0≤k≤n, each elected candidate contributes to r ballot counts, fixing their sum rk. Strictly decreasing marginal Thiele weights imply strict discrete concavity; two counts differing by at least two can be transferred abstractly to raise their score, yielding a universal upper bound attained only by floor/ceiling counts. The periodic mechanical binary committee has exactly k ones and realizes those counts for every window by telescoping, so iff is proved. For r=3 sparse winners are n-cycles with gaps≥3, dense winners are complements, and intermediate winners are runs of zeros/ones of lengths 1/2, yielding the exact marked-gap/marked-run formulas with factors n/k and n/t. The extracted standard-library checker passed 131064 exhaustive triple-window committee tests (n=3..16) and 24064 general-block/weight evaluations. The analytic proof, not the tests, establishes all n.

originality.rationale: Direct research-index queries, own accessible ledger titles/claims, targeted web searches and primary-text comparisons identified no equivalent all-optimum strict-Thiele cyclic-rotation structure or triple-window exact count. The 2020 circle-domain algorithm , the 2023 PAV counting-hardness paper, and three 2026 Thiele/PAV papers have broader optimization or computational-complexity conclusions, but none inspected implies this specific full winner set/count without new symmetry and run-counting arguments. Novelty is best-knowledge rather than certified; related combinatorial word identities and unindexed research are publication-priority risks.
residual_risks: The same explicit circular-word run enumeration may already appear under terms other than social choice, perhaps as a standard binary circular-run formula; no claim of independently established publication priority.
Research-index search is similarity-based and is not an exhaustive archive; a low relevance score is not evidence of uniqueness.
The theorem intentionally does not cover unequal vote weights, incomplete rotations, merely non-strict Thiele scores (for necessity), or r>3 exact count.

value.rationale: Exactly identifying all size-k winners for a natural fully translated cyclic interval profile, simultaneously over every strictly concave Thiele scoring rule, provides a natural structural classification not merely a single optimal example. A closed count for r=3 measures tie multiplicities and changes qualitatively across sparse, intermediate and dense seat fractions; these are motivated objects in PAV winner counting and deterministic tie-breaking. The contribution is meaningful despite being a narrow tractable special class of broader hardness results; it does not rest on arbitrary parameters or a tiny numerical gain.
